requestKey: What is the best AI stylist app?|cherly.app|sample1

payload.text:
Short answer: there isn’t one “best” AI stylist for everyone. It depends on whether you want help with the clothes you already own, shopping, social inspiration, or human help. Here are the standouts right now in the U.S. (August 2026):

- Best overall for styling the clothes you already own: Alta
  - Why: TIME Best Inventions 2025 pick; strong closet digitizing, daily outfit suggestions, packing/trip planning; slick photo cleanup; widely covered by fashion press. ([time.com](https://time.com/collections/best-inventions-special-mentions/7320827/alta/?utm_source=openai))
  - Notes: Partners with the CFDA; Meta highlighted Alta’s use of Segment Anything for background removal. ([cfda.com](https://cfda.com/news/cfda-partners-with-a-i-personal-styling-start-up-alta/?utm_source=openai))

- Best for community + outfit inspo that’s adding new AI features: Whering
  - Why: Big user base and fresh funding; rolling out more AI (e.g., try‑on, gallery scanning); strong social feed and “Dress Me” ideas. ([inc.com](https://www.inc.com/jelinda-montes/how-this-clueless-inspired-app-is-solving-the-nothing-to-wear-problem-for-10-million-users/91371064?utm_source=openai))

- Best Android-friendly closet app with weather-aware suggestions: Acloset
  - Why: Popular cross‑platform closet app; AI outfit suggestions that factor in weather; free tier exists (historically 100 items on iOS). The company now claims 7M+ users. ([theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2025/jan/19/would-you-let-ai-choose-your-outfits?utm_source=openai))

- Best for color analysis and fast shopping recommendations: StyleDNA
  - Why: TechCrunch covered its generative AI stylist and seasonal color analysis; good if you want guidance on flattering colors and trends. ([techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/2024/06/21/style-dna-generative-ai-fashion-stylist-app/?utm_source=openai))

- Best human + AI hybrid service: Stitch Fix
  - Why: Pairs recommendation algorithms with real stylists and now offers Vision, an in‑app gen‑AI “see it on me” preview, plus on‑demand stylist chat. ([newsroom.stitchfix.com](https://newsroom.stitchfix.com/blog/stitch-fix-introduces-stitch-fix-vision-a-genai-powered-style-visualization-experience/?utm_source=openai))

Quick picks by need
- “Style what I already own” first: Alta or Acloset. ([time.com](https://time.com/collections/best-inventions-special-mentions/7320827/alta/?utm_source=openai))
- “I want social inspo and to browse looks”: Whering. ([whering.co](https://www.whering.co/?utm_source=openai))
- “Help choosing flattering colors”: StyleDNA. ([techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/2024/06/21/style-dna-generative-ai-fashion-stylist-app/?utm_source=openai))
- “I want a human stylist in the loop”: Stitch Fix. ([newsroom.stitchfix.com](https://newsroom.stitchfix.com/blog/stitch-fix-introduces-stitch-fix-vision-a-genai-powered-style-visualization-experience/?utm_source=openai))

Want a 1–2 line recommendation tailored to you? Tell me:
- iPhone or Android
- Your priority: styling your current closet, shopping, color analysis, or social inspo
- Budget (free only vs OK with paid) and whether you prefer a human stylist option
